# Per-terrain-type visual enhancement — design plan (2026-07-31)

> **Status:** DESIGN ONLY. No production code was changed producing this document.
> **Audience:** implementation agents. Every integration point below was verified by
> reading the file named. Citations are `path:symbol` or `path:line` — line numbers were
> read at the commit this doc was written against; **anchor on the SYMBOL and re-grep if
> a line has drifted.**
> **Water is OUT OF SCOPE** — a parallel agent owns terrain codes 16-20, 22 and 23
> (see §3.8 for the interaction contract only).

---

## §0 — How to use this document

1. Read §1 (terrain table) and find your family.
2. Read §2 (shared foundation). **Wave 0 must land before any family wave.** If you are a
   family agent and `scene3d/terrain_oracle.js` does not exist, stop and say so.
3. Read §2.6 — **the traps**. Four of them will silently waste a day each.
   Then read §2.7 — the BC7 texture arm you are matching, the parallax occlusion mapping
   already on the ground, and the atlased-statics wall that silently erases attributes and
   material patches. Background: `docs/HANDOFF-relief-v2-2026-07-31.md` (repo root).
4. Read your family section in §3: exact files, flags, quality behaviour, landblock
   lifecycle handling, perf budget, tests.
5. Read §5 (invariants). Violating one is an automatic revert; three of them are
   **mechanically enforced and will throw at registration time**.
6. Ship flagged-OFF. Promote to default-ON only after the §6 bar.

---

## §1 — The terrain table (codes 0..31) and effect families

### 1.1 Three sources, one truth

| Source | What it gives | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `ac-headers/acclient.h` `enum LandDefs::TerrainType` (≈:4112) | Retail C++ enum: **0..0x14 named, 0x15..0x1F = `Reserved21`..`Reserved31`, 0x20 = `RoadType`** | The *engine* enum. Codes 21-31 are unnamed in the shipped executable. |
| `apps/holtburger-web/data/terrain_palette.json` → `palette[]`, 32 entries | Generated by `cargo run -p holtburger-dat --example dump_terrain_palette` from `client_portal.dat` file `0x13000000` (Region) → `TerrainDesc.terrain_types[].terrain_name`. `_region_name: "Dereth"`, `_terrain_type_count: 32`. | **The names of record.** The DAT *does* name 21-31. |
| `scene3d/terrain.js` `TERRAIN_CODE_TO_RGB` (:105) and `TERRAIN_CODE_TO_DETAIL_SLICE` (:577) | The client's per-code LUTs, keyed 0..31 | Names match the DAT exactly. Mirror their style for any new per-code LUT. |

`crates/holtburger-dat/src/file_type/region.rs:907 struct TerrainType { terrain_name,
terrain_color, scene_types }` is the parser. **`terrain_color` is the radar/minimap
colour, not a render tint** (documented at region.rs ≈:653) — do not use it to pick VFX
colours. `data/terrain_palette.json` is loaded at runtime by `terrain.js:448
loadTerrainPaletteLut()` into a 32×1 RGBA `DataTexture` (`TERRAIN_PALETTE_LENGTH = 32`,
:424) for the `?terrainPalette` tint.

Terrain code is 5 bits — `terrain.js:145` masks `& 0x1f`. Road rides a separate channel
(`userData.roadCodes` → `uVertexTypes.G`), so `RoadType (0x20)` never appears in the
terrain-code stream.

**The client already has a water-code set and it is wider than the enum suggests.**
`terrain.js:788 TERRAIN_WATER_CODES` defaults to `{16,17,18,19,20,22,23}` — **code 23
(`SeaSlime`) is treated as water today**, and `?strictWaterCodes` *drops* 22 and 23.
`terrain.js:793 TERRAIN_LAVA_CODES` is an **empty Set** (Region `0x13` ships no lava
codes), so the vertex shader's lava-displacement branch is dead in Dereth. Both are
exported and consumed as GPU bitmasks via `terrain.js:2296 computeCodeBitmask(codeSet)`
→ `uWaterCodeMask` / `uLavaCodeMask`.

### 1.3 Family sets (Wave 0 deliverable — one shared module, not per-effect)

```js
// scene3d/terrain_families.js
export const FAM_NONE    = 0;
export const FAM_GRASS   = 1;   // 1, 3, 9, 21, 28, 29
export const FAM_SAND    = 2;   // 10, 11, 12
export const FAM_ROCK    = 3;   // 0, 13, 14, 30
export const FAM_SNOWICE = 4;   // 2, 15, 27
export const FAM_SWAMP   = 5;   // 4  (+ 23 ONLY under ?strictWaterCodes — see §3.8.3)
export const FAM_VOLCANO = 6;   // 6, 25, 26
export const FAM_DIRT    = 7;   // 5, 7, 8, 24, 31
export const FAM_WATER   = 8;   // 16,17,18,19,20,22,23 — OWNED BY THE WATER AGENT
```
Ship it as a `Uint8Array(32)` code→family LUT plus the named constants. Sub-variants that
matter to a family's tuning (forestfloor vs Grassland, Volcano1 vs ObsidianPlain) are a
per-code parameter table **inside** the family module, not a separate family.

**The family LUT must derive its water membership from `TERRAIN_WATER_CODES`**, not from
a hardcoded list, so `?strictWaterCodes` stays consistent across the whole client.

⚠ **Family membership is a property of the CODE, not of the texture.** Retail shares one
RenderSurface across `BarrenRock (0) + Argila (24) + DesolateLands (31)` and across
`PatchyGrassland (9) + Moss (28)` — codes that land in *different* families here. See
§2.7.2 before writing any "what kind of ground is this" logic.

## §2 — Shared foundation (WAVE 0 — blocks everything)

### 2.1 `scene3d/terrain_oracle.js` — terrain code + ground height at world (x, y)

**Do not invent this. Generalise the proven one.** `scene3d/audio/ambient_runtime.js`
already samples terrain code at the player's position to drive ambient audio.

Reference implementation: `ambient_runtime.js:670 _sampleTerrainVertex(player)` →
`{code, vertexIndex, lbX, lbY} | null`; thin wrapper `:656 _sampleTerrainCodeAt(player)`
→ `code | -1`. Constants at the top of that file: `VERTEX_GRID = 9`,
`VERTEX_SPACING_M = 24.0`, `METERS_PER_LANDBLOCK = 192.0`. Mesh source is injectable
(`_getTerrainMeshes`), wired at `scene3d/index.js:5355`:
```js
getTerrainMeshes: () => terrainGroup.children,
```

The load-bearing arithmetic:
```js
const lbX = Math.floor(x / 192), lbY = Math.floor(y / 192);
// find mesh in terrainGroup.children with ud.lbX === lbX && ud.lbY === lbY
const codes = mesh.userData.terrainCodes;            // Uint8Array(81)
const col = clamp(Math.round((x - lbX*192) / 24), 0, 8);
const row = clamp(Math.round((y - lbY*192) / 24), 0, 8);
const code = codes[col * 9 + row] | 0;               // COLUMN-MAJOR
```

**Where the data is stashed** — `scene3d/terrain.js`, LB mesh builder, ending
`scene3d.terrainGroup.add(lbMesh)` (:4207):
```js
const lbMesh = new THREE.Mesh(geom, material);                              // :4103
lbMesh.name = `terrain-lb-${lbX.toString(16)}-${lbY.toString(16)}`;         // :4104
lbMesh.position.set(lbX * 192, lbY * 192, 0);                               // :4116
lbMesh.userData = {                                                         // :4139
  lbX, lbY, lbId: ((lbX << 24) | (lbY << 16) | 0xffff) >>> 0,
  heightMin, heightMax,
  vertexTypesTexture, mergeDataTexture,
  terrainCodes: terrainCodesCopy,   // Uint8Array(81), column-major
  roadCodes: roadCodesCopy, hasRoads,
  detailNormalEnabled, detailNormalSlice,
  triplanarEnabled, triplanarSharpness, triplanarSlopeLo, triplanarSlopeHi,
  subdivLevel: effectiveSubdiv,     // 1 | 2 | 4 | 8
  displacementEnabled, waterCodeMask, lavaCodeMask,
};
```
Source is `Uint8Array.from(wasmMesh.terrainCodes)` (`terrain.js:3662`). The wasm struct is
`apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:1554 pub struct LandblockMesh` with getters
`positions` (:1576, `Float32Array(243)`), `indices` (:1583), `terrainCodes` (:1591,
`Uint8Array(81)`), `roadCodes` (:1599), `heightMin`/`heightMax` (:1606/:1613),
`terrainMergeData` (:1622), and — **already present, use it** —
`heights` (:1631, `Float32Array(81)`, `idx = vx*9 + vy`).

**Coordinate frame.** Terrain geometry is LB-local `x,y ∈ [0,192]`, `z` = height; the
mesh is translated to `(lbX*192, lbY*192, 0)`. `worldRoot` carries `rotation.x = -π/2`,
so **inside `terrainGroup` you are in AC space: +X east, +Y north, +Z up.** Parent every
terrain-VFX object under `terrainGroup` (or a sibling with the same transform) and use AC
coordinates directly. `adapter.js:1732 acToThree(ax, ay, az) → [ax, az, -ay]` is only for
objects outside `worldRoot`.

**Ground height, exact, from wasm:**
```
SessionHandle.terrainHeightAt(world_x: number, world_y: number): number | undefined
```
`pkg/holtburger_web.d.ts:5893`, binding `src/lib.rs:35045`. Mirrors
`crates/holtburger-world/src/state/types.rs:958 WorldState::terrain_height_at` — **triangle
plane on the retail per-cell diagonal** (`holtburger_dat::terrain_subdiv::cell_swto_ne_cut`
+ `triangle_height_in_cell`), so it tracks the *drawn* surface. `undefined` for an LB not
in the cache. Existing callers: `camera.js:1337` (camera ground lift), `entities.js:46`
(`?groundClamp`). Fed by `SessionHandle.populateTerrain(landblock_id, heights,
terrain_codes)` (d.ts:5165), called from `index.html:4219`.

> ⚠ **`populateTerrain` throws the codes away.** `WorldState::populate_terrain_water`
> (`crates/holtburger-world/src/state/types.rs:571`) reduces the 81 codes to
> `[bool; 81]` water flags. There is **no** wasm terrain-code-at-(x,y) export and
> `is_entirely_water_cell_at` is not bound. `RegionJs.terrainNameForCode(code)`
> (d.ts:2836) is a name lookup, not a spatial query. **The JS userData path is the only
> terrain-code query.** Do not spend time looking for a wasm one.

#### 2.1.1 The oracle owns its own cache — **this is not optional**

`landblock_lru.js:1519-1543 park()` **removes the terrain mesh from `terrainGroup`** (it
stashes it in `p.terrain` and re-adds on `unpark()`). Park is default-ON and **replaces
eviction once the LRU is at cap**. A scanner that walks `terrainGroup.children` therefore
returns `null` for every parked LB — which, at cap, is most of the ring. `ambient_runtime`
tolerates this (one sample/tick, audio just goes quiet); **a VFX oracle must not.**

So the oracle keeps `Map<lbKey, {codes: Uint8Array(81), heights: Float32Array(81), lbX,
lbY}>`, populated **once at bake** and retained across park/unpark, cleared **only** on
evict/rebake. Two `Uint8Array(81)` + `Float32Array(81)` per LB ≈ 405 bytes; at the 256-slot
LRU cap that is ~104 KB. Free.

Wave 0A therefore adds **one line** to the `lbMesh.userData` literal in `terrain.js`:
```js
heights: Float32Array.from(wasmMesh.heights),   // 81, column-major idx = vx*9 + vy
```
and ports `cell_swto_ne_cut` to JS. Constants verbatim from
`crates/holtburger-dat/src/terrain_subdiv.rs:383` — **u32 wraparound throughout; use
`Math.imul` and `>>> 0`, never widen to a double:**
```
inner = 214614067 * gx + 1813693831                 (u32 wrap)
v8    = gy * inner - 1109124029 * gx - 1369149221    (u32 wrap)
SWtoNEcut = (v8 >>> 0) * 2.3283064e-10 >= 0.5
gx = lbX * 8 + cellX ;  gy = lbY * 8 + cellY
```
The JS port is validated **against `terrainHeightAt`** (§2.5) — that is the whole reason
the wasm function stays the reference.

#### 2.1.2 Module API

```js
// scene3d/terrain_oracle.js
export function createTerrainOracle({ getTerrainMeshes });

// oracle.noteLandblock(lbKey, { codes, heights, lbX, lbY })  // called at bake
// oracle.invalidate(lbKey)                                   // evict / rebake ONLY
// oracle.sample(x, y) -> null | {
//   code,        // 0..31, nearest-vertex snap (matches ambient_runtime semantics)
//   family,      // FAM_* from terrain_families.js
//   height,      // exact, split-diagonal triangle interp
//   normal,      // {x,y,z} unit, same triangle plane
//   lbX, lbY, lbKey,
//   cornerCodes, // [sw, se, nw, ne] — for feathering at type boundaries
// }
// oracle.sampleCode(x, y) -> -1 | 0..31         // cheap path, no height
// oracle.familyCoverage(lbKey) -> Uint16Array(9) // vertex counts per FAM_*
// oracle.stats() -> {cached, hits, misses, parkedHits}
```
`getTerrainMeshes` remains as a **backfill** for LBs baked before the oracle existed
(scan once, cache, never scan again).

`lbKey` is the canonical residency key — reuse the exported helpers rather than
re-deriving: `landblock_lru.js:348 lbKeyFromXY(lbX, lbY)` = `((lbX & 0xff) << 24) |
((lbY & 0xff) << 16)`, and `:352 lbKeyOf(landblockIdOrLbKey)`, both exported at
`landblock_lru.js:1886`. World origin = `((lbKey >>> 24) & 0xff) * 192`,
`((lbKey >>> 16) & 0xff) * 192`. Note `userData.lbId` uses the `| 0xffff` cell form —
mask it with `lbKeyOf` before using it as a residency key.

### 2.2 `scene3d/terrain_vfx.js` — the per-landblock spawn/despawn spine

One module owns landblock lifecycle so no family agent touches `landblock_lru.js` or
`fixed_grid.js`.

```js
export function registerTerrainVfx(provider);
// provider = {
//   id: "terrain.grass", families: [FAM_GRASS],
//   scope: "landblock" | "camera",
//   enabled(): boolean,            // the ?flag reader (§2.4)
//   quality(flags): object|null,   // null => disabled at this tier
//   onLandblockReady(ctx),         // {lbKey, lbX, lbY, oracle, group, quality}
//   onLandblockPark(lbKey), onLandblockUnpark(lbKey, ctx),
//   onLandblockGone(lbKey),
//   update(dt, frameCtx),          // {playerPos, camera, wind, weather, sky, tSec}
//   dispose(),
// }
export function terrainVfxTick(dt, frameCtx);
export function terrainVfxStats();     // -> window.__terrainVfx
```

**Two scopes, deliberately:**

* `scope: "landblock"` — objects created when an LB's terrain lands, destroyed when it
  goes. Correct for sparse, wide-area things: volcano embers, marsh fireflies, dust
  devils.
* `scope: "camera"` — a **fixed-size pool re-centred on the player each frame**, never
  allocated per LB. Correct for dense near-field things: **grass**. The default 13×13 ring
  is ~1.15 km across; per-LB grass is not affordable. The pool covers radius `R`
  (default 48 m); blades leaving the ring are re-scattered on the leading edge and
  re-sampled through the oracle. **Camera scope is immune to evict/park/rebake entirely.**

#### 2.2.1 Lifecycle seams — verified, including the two traps

| Event | Seam | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **attach** | **No event exists.** `terrain.js:4207` is a bare `scene3d.terrainGroup.add(lbMesh)`. | Hook by wrapping `scene3d/index.js:3076 loadTerrainForLandblock(lbX, lbY, prefetchedMesh)` — it returns `lbMesh` or `null`. Do **not** monkey-patch `terrainGroup.add`. |
| **evict** | `landblock_lru.js:1097 evict(lbKey)`; step 1 at :1108-1122 filters `terrainGroup.children` on `ud.lbX/ud.lbY`, removes, and **disposes** the tracked disposables. Callback fires at **:1413** `this._onEvictLandblock(lbKey)`, wired at `scene3d/index.js:4849`. | The only built-in callback. |
| **park** | `landblock_lru.js:1486 park(lbKey)`; step ① at :1519-1543 stashes into `p.terrain`, removes from `terrainGroup`, calls `s._parkTerrainBatchForLb(lbKey)`. **Nothing disposed.** | ⚠ **`_onEvictLandblock` is deliberately NOT fired** (comment at :1638). **A provider hooked only to the evict callback leaks on every park** — and park *replaces* eviction at cap. |
| **unpark** | `landblock_lru.js:1658 unpark(lbKey)` re-attaches the stashed containers, calls `s._unparkTerrainBatchForLb(lbKey, meshes)`. | Restore visibility; **never re-scatter** (hash-stable placement, §5.4). |
| **incoming / vacated sets** | `fixed_grid.js:270 FixedSlotGrid.update(cx, cy)` → `{moved, teleport, seed, incoming: Set<lbKey>, vacated: Set<lbKey>}`. Wired at `scene3d/index.js:4941`; `EdgeParkScheduler.onVacated/onResident` at `fixed_grid.js:471/489`. | The cleanest existing per-LB signal, but it fires only on LB crossings and sits behind `?fixedGrid`. Use as a cross-check, not the primary. |
| **rebake** | `terrain.js:3530 tickTerrainLodRebake(scene3d, currentLbKey)` destroys and rebuilds the LB mesh. | Treat as gone-then-ready; `oracle.invalidate(lbKey)` first. |

**Install the hooks on every facade.** `terrain_batch.js:548 _installHooksOn` /
`:563 _installHooks` is the precedent and the comment there documents the dual-facade
footgun: install `_evict…` / `_park…` / `_unpark…ForLb` function properties on
`scene3d`, `scene3d.landblockLru.scene3d`, **and** `window.liveScene3d`. Copy that
pattern exactly.

#### 2.2.2 Particle-owning providers use the owner registry — and the key helper exists

`scene3d/particles/owner_registry.js`: `:142 async addEmitter(ownerKey, manager, req)`,
`:302 destroyAllForOwner(ownerKey)`, `:262 stopEmitter`, `:233 destroyEmitter`,
`:281 destroySome`, `:102 emitterCountForOwner`, singleton
`export const ownerRegistry` (:339). Handles are **epoch-guarded** so a stale handle
cannot destroy a rebuilt owner's emitter.

**Use the existing landblock owner-key helper:**
`scene3d/vfx/particle_attach.js:191 staticOwnerKeyForLb(landblockId)`. Do not invent a
second key scheme — statics already own emitters under it.

Despawn is then one call: `ownerRegistry.destroyAllForOwner(staticOwnerKeyForLb(lbId))`.
Park should `stopEmitter` (or set `intensity`/emission to 0), **never** `.visible = false`
(§5.3).

The underlying manager call is `particles/particle_manager.js:936 async addEmitter(req)`:
```js
req = {
  emitterInfo,   // wasm ParticleEmitterJs OR a POJO with the same camelCase fields
  parent,        // PhysicsObj-like anchor {position, quaternion, partFrames?}
  partIndex,     // -1 = whole object
  parentOffset,  // {position, quaternion} — snapshotted BY VALUE before any await
  emitterId,     // 0 => assigned
  blocking,      // retail CreateBlockingParticleEmitter semantics
}  // -> Promise<emitterId>, 0 on failure
```

### 2.3 Shared inputs — read these, do not fork them

| Input | Accessor (verified) |
|---|---|
| **Player world pos (three space)** | `scene3d.cameraSwitcher.getPlayerWorldPosition(out: THREE.Vector3) → Vector3\|null` — `camera.js:2582`. Rotation-invariant; `lighting.js` already uses it for its nearest-light pool. |
| **Player world pos (AC space, +Z up)** | `camera.js:2590 _safePlayerPos() → {x,y,z}` (integrator → `getPlayerWorldPos()` → LB-centre fallback). Smoothed mirror: `cameraSwitcher.predictedPlayerPos` (`camera.js:485`). Raw pose→world: `scene3d/rust_pose.js:70 rustPoseWorldFromPose(pose)`. |
| **Current LB** | `scene3d.playerLbKey`; `landblockLru.getCurrentLbId()` (rig-derived, fresh across teleports — `index.js:4867`). |
| **Frame clock** | `scene3d.frameTime.tsSec` — the single time source. `loop.js:919 tickTerrainUTime` and `:949 tickVfxOscillators` both read it. Never call `performance.now()` in an effect. |
| **Shared VFX uniforms** | `scene3d/materials.js:415 VFX_GLOBALS = { uTime, uWindDir (Vector2), uWetness, uFrost, uCamPos (Vector3) }` — bound **by reference** into every patched material. ⚠ `uCamPos` is **declared but never written by anything** — if you need it, write it from `loop.js` and say so in the PR. |
| **Wind (live, weather-driven)** | `scene3d/vfx/weather_inputs.js:114 writeWindVector(t, stormness, out)` — writes `VFX_GLOBALS.uWindDir.value` each frame from `loop.js:973 tickVfxWeatherInputs`. Direction wanders; gust = sum of incommensurate sines (0.37/0.91/1.73 Hz), deterministic, no `Math.random`. Snapshot: `getWeatherInputs() → {wetness, frost, stormness, windDir:{x,y}, windDirDeg}`. |
| **Wind (static, tree flags)** | `scene3d/tree_wind.js:33 treeWindEnabled()`, `:46 treeWindStrength()` (0..4), `:53 treeWindDir()` (default **135° = SE**). GPU sway component: `vfx/components/windSwayGpu.js`, uniforms `uWindAmp`, `uWindFreq`, `uWindDir2` (**object-space**), `uWindBaseZ`, `uWindFlutter`. |
| **Weather (zero-alloc)** | `scene3d/weather_state.js readWeatherVfxInputs(out)` → `{is_storm, temperature_C, season}`. Change detection: `getWeatherRevision()`. Forcing flags live in `scene3d/weather/manager.js:30 parseUrlOverrides()`. |
| **Sky / sun / time-of-day** | `window.liveScene3d.skyLightingController._lastState` — the once-per-frame cached snapshot (`sky_lighting.js:44 snapshotSkyState`): `{dirColorArgb, dirBright, dirHeading, dirPitch, ambColorArgb, ambBright, fogColorArgb, fogMin, fogMax, worldFog, timeOfDayNormalized, dayGroupIndex}`. **Never call `getSkyState()` yourself** — one wasm call per frame is the contract. Conversion to an AC sun vector: `loop.js:1012 tickTerrainSunDir`. |
| **Environmental gates** | `scene3d/vfx/particle_env.js readParticleEnv(scene3d, out)`; gates `scene3d/vfx/particle_env_gates.js` — `nightFactor(sunAlt)`, `pollenGate`, `firefliesGate`, `leavesGate`, `breathFogGate`, frozen `PARTICLE_GATES`. **A gated-out component synthesises no emitter at all** — as cheap as flag-off. |

### 2.4 URL flags — the mandatory idiom

`docs/url-flags.md` (2026-07-23 box) is explicit:
> *"an opt-in reader must be an exact-match check (`=== "1"` / `=== "on"` /
> truthy-on-a-specific-string), **never `!== "off"`**"*

The audit found **20 silently-LIVE** `!== "off"` readers still documented as `off`.

**The reference implementation is `scene3d/gfx_relief.js:99 resolveGfxRelief(search,
presetFlags)`.** It is the full house form — strict exact-match master flag *plus* a
quality-preset fallback, which is exactly what a quality-tiered terrain effect needs:

```js
// scene3d/gfx_relief.js:122 — "master flag: STRICT exact-match opt-in (never `!== "off"`)"
const rawMaster = params.get("gfxRelief");
let enabled, enabledSource;
if (rawMaster === "on")       { enabled = true;  enabledSource = "url"; }
else if (rawMaster === "off") { enabled = false; enabledSource = "url"; }
else {
  enabled = base.gfxRelief === true;              // quality-preset value wins when absent
  enabledSource = flags ? "preset" : "fallback";
  if (rawMaster !== null) {
    console.warn(`[gfxRelief] ignoring ?gfxRelief=${JSON.stringify(rawMaster)} — the master `
      + `flag is an EXACT-match opt-in; use ?gfxRelief=on (or =off).`);
  }
}
```
Three details to copy, not just the shape:
* `base = {...GFX_RELIEF_FALLBACK, ...(presetFlags || getQuality().flags)}` — the preset
  supplies the default, the URL overrides it, and a hardcoded fallback covers Node/early
  init.
* **An unrecognised value warns loudly and does NOT enable.** *"a silent no-op here looks
  exactly like a broken Rust decode."*
* The flag is **deliberately kept out of `quality.js BOOL_FLAGS`** so `parseBool` cannot
  widen `=== "on"` to `1`/`true`/`yes`. **Every terrain-VFX master flag in this plan must do
  the same.** Numeric knobs (`terrainGrassDensity`, `terrainGrassRadius`) *do* belong in
  `INT_FLAGS`/`FLOAT_FLAGS`.
* It returns a `source: {enabled, subdivLevel, scale}` provenance object — copy that too;
  it makes "why is my flag off?" a one-line console read.

Two shorter readers, for effects with no preset fallback — **copy one verbatim**:

```js
// SAFE OPT-IN — scene3d/tree_wind.js:33
let _flag;
export function treeWindEnabled() {
  if (_flag !== undefined) return _flag;
  let on = false;                              // DEFAULT OFF
  const v = _strFlag("treeWind");
  if (v != null) {
    const s = v.toLowerCase();
    on = s === "on" || s === "1" || s === "true" || s === "yes";
  }
  return (_flag = on);
}

// DEFAULT-ON OPT-OUT (only after promotion) — scene3d/vfx_catalog.js:27
export function visualEnabled() {
  if (_flag !== undefined) return _flag;
  let on = true;
  const v = _strFlag("visual");
  if (v != null) {
    const s = v.toLowerCase();
    on = s !== "off" && s !== "0" && s !== "false" && s !== "no" && s !== "";
  }
  return (_flag = on);
}
```
The shared helpers (`_strFlag` / `_boolFlag(name, def)` / `_numFlag(name, def, min, max)`)
live at `scene3d/vfx_flags.js:43`/`:52` — `_boolFlag` returns `def` when the param is
absent, which is the correct behaviour for both directions.

**The firewall composition rule** (`vfx_flags.js` header): an effect is active iff
`visualEnabled() && <its per-effect flag>`. Register each new flag in
`VFX_EFFECT_FLAGS` (the frozen componentId→reader router) so `vfxEffectEnabled(id)`
resolves it; unknown ids fall back to `visualAllEffects()`.

**Hard gate: `scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs`.** It parses `docs/url-flags.md` rows and sweeps
`index.html` + `scene3d/**/*.js`, exiting 1 on `UNDOCUMENTED`, `NO-READER`,
`OFF-SPELLING` or `PRESENCE-GUARD`. **A PR without a docs row fails.** Run
`node scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs --app apps/holtburger-web`. Fill the **Reader** column.

Master kill switch: `?terrainVfx=off`. Each family keeps its own switch plus numeric
knobs in the `?foliageParticleRadius` style (documented at
`vfx/components/foliageAmbient.js:86 _foliageDrawRadiusM`).

`vfx_flags.js visualBudget()` is a **parsed-but-unconsumed** governor stub (default
`Infinity`) reserved for a cost model. A terrain-VFX cost model would be its first
consumer — a nice-to-have, not a Wave-0 requirement.

### 2.5 Wave 0 tests

`test_terrain_families.mjs`
* All 32 codes → exactly one family. Water membership is **derived from
  `TERRAIN_WATER_CODES`**, and flipping `?strictWaterCodes` moves code 23 from
  `FAM_WATER` to `FAM_SWAMP` and code 22 out of `FAM_WATER`.
* Deltas vs `TERRAIN_CODE_TO_DETAIL_SLICE` are asserted explicitly (6/25/26 STONE→VOLCANO,
  4 NONE→SWAMP) so an edit to either table trips.

`test_terrain_oracle.mjs`
* Column-major: a code planted at `codes[3*9 + 5]` returns for
  `(lbX*192 + 3*24, lbY*192 + 5*24)`.
* Nearest-vertex snap and `[0,8]` clamping at LB edges.
* `sample()` → `null` for an unknown LB and for a mesh missing `terrainCodes`.
* **Park survival:** `noteLandblock` then remove the mesh from the fake `terrainGroup`
  (simulating park) → `sample()` still resolves. `invalidate()` then returns `null`.
* **`cell_swto_ne_cut` parity** against the Rust test vectors at
  `crates/holtburger-dat/src/terrain_subdiv.rs:1453`, plus a `gx` large enough that a
  naive double-precision port would diverge (proves `Math.imul`).
* Height continuity across a cell boundary: `|Δz| < 1e-4` either side of `x = 24`.

`test_terrain_vfx_lifecycle.mjs`
* `onLandblockReady` once per LB; `onLandblockGone` once on evict.
* **Park does NOT fire `onLandblockGone`** — it fires `onLandblockPark`; unpark restores
  with identical first-object placement (hash stability).
* `scope:"camera"` provider allocates its pool once across 100 simulated moves.
* Hooks are installed on all three facades (`scene3d`, `landblockLru.scene3d`,
  `liveScene3d`).

**Live check (the single most important validation in this plan):** `?nosw=1`,
headless login, then
`window.__terrainVfx.oracleSelfTest()` — 500 random points in the resident ring, asserting
`oracle.sample(x,y).height` agrees with `window.__sessionHandle.terrainHeightAt(x,y)`
within 1e-3 wherever both resolve. Every family stands on this.

### 2.6 ⚠ Four traps that will each cost you a day

**T1 — `uWindDir` on the terrain material is dead.** `terrain.js:3882` sets
`uWindDir = new THREE.Vector2(1, 0)` **at material build and never ticks it**; its only
consumers are the sand-UV rotation lines (:2050, :2055-2070). It is **unrelated to**
`VFX_GLOBALS.uWindDir`. If you want live wind on terrain, wire it in `loop.js` next to
`tickTerrainUTime` (`loop.js:919`, which walks `scene3d.terrainMaterials`) and say so.

**T2 — there is no player position on the terrain material.** The terrain fragment shader
uses only three's built-in `cameraPosition` (`terrain.js:1593`, `:2179`). Any
player-proximity terrain shader effect (grass stomp reading the trail map is fine — that's
a texture; a *distance-to-player* term is not) needs a new uniform pushed from `loop.js`.

**T3 — the shader does not read the `terrainCode` attribute on the subdiv path.**
The per-vertex `terrainCode` attribute is created in **`adapter.js:327`** (base) and
**`:391`** (subdiv) — *not* in `terrain.js`:
```js
geom.setAttribute("terrainCode", new THREE.BufferAttribute(terrainCodes, 1, false));
```
but `terrain.js:3669-3672` records that on the subdivided path it is *"unused by the
current shader (kept on the geometry for forward compat)"*. The fragment shader reads the
**9×9 `uVertexTypes` DataTexture** instead (`terrain.js:1052`, built by
`adapter.js:724 buildVertexTypesDataTexture`, which **transposes** the column-major
source; `terrain.js:1434 vertexTypeAt(iu, iv)`, `:1383 atlasUvFor(code, cellUv)` where
`.z` is the atlas layer). The *vertex* shader **does** read `in float terrainCode` for the
water/lava displacement branch (`terrain.js:929`). **If your effect needs the code in the
fragment stage, use `uVertexTypes`, not the attribute.**

Also: `terrain_batch.js:650` whitelists exactly
`["position", "normal", "terrainCode"]` (+ optional `vertexBrightness/Saturate/Hue`,
`acLightNormal`) and synthesises `aLbSlot` (:678). **A new terrain geometry attribute that
is not on that whitelist silently vanishes under `?terrainBatch=on`** (default-on).

**T4 — the composer uses a logarithmic depth buffer.** `logarithmicDepthBuffer` is enabled
at `scene3d/index.js:768`. A custom pmndrs `Effect` receives **raw** log-encoded depth and
must decode it:
```glsl
float dist = exp2(2.0 * depth / hbLogDepthFC) - 1.0;   // sky pixels: depth >= 0.9999
```
Working template in-tree: `HorizonDissolveEffect` at `scene3d/atmosphere_pipeline.js:141`.
Treating log depth as linear places geometry at a wildly wrong distance. Also honour the
`OPTICAL_EFFECTS_HANDOFF.md` rule for depth reads on the R9 290: **NEAREST filtering and
a sentinel-aware threshold**.

### 2.7 The texture arm, the existing ground detail, and the atlased-statics wall

Context: `docs/HANDOFF-relief-v2-2026-07-31.md` (repo root `docs/`, **not** app `docs/`).
Read it before Wave 1 — it is the state of the ground-detail programme these effects sit
on top of.

#### 2.7.1 There are TWO mutually exclusive terrain texture arms. Be agnostic to both.

| Arm | Flag | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| CC0 / "plain" | `?pbrTerrain` (**default**) | curated ambientCG art replacing 26 of the 33 layers |
| **Retail BC7** | `?terrainBc7=on` (**strict `=== on/1/true/yes/512/1024`**) | the art AC shipped: retail terrain RenderSurfaces, ×4 `realesrgan-x4plus`, BC7 with full mip chains, `nra` derived from the retail albedo |

They **both write the same layers' albedo and are mutually exclusive** — when `terrainBc7`
wins, the CC0 load is skipped and `pbrTerrainState` is fed the derived BC7 `nra`
(`scene3d/terrain_bc7.js` header; `docs/url-flags.md` `terrainBc7` row). BC7 is
capability-gated on `EXT_texture_compression_bptc` via `bc7Available()`, so a GPU without
BPTC behaves exactly like flag-off.

**The look target for every effect in this plan is the BC7 arm**: statics `?texBc7=on` +
terrain `?terrainBc7=on`, served on **:8767** (`/mnt/wbterminal2/bc7-v2-rebake/serve/
serve-hires-bc7.sh`, unified dist `/mnt/wbterminal2/holtburger-dist-hires-bc7m`, 888,137
shards / 2,999 tex-bc7 records). The default **:8765** shows the CC0 arm.

**Design rule:** tune colours, sparkle thresholds and emissive strengths against the BC7
arm, but **never assume an arm**. No effect may read a texture, a layer index or an
`nra` channel to decide *what kind of ground this is*. If you need "is this snow", ask the
oracle for the **code**.

#### 2.7.2 Retail SHARES RenderSurfaces across terrain codes — key off CODE, never texture

The 33 terrain layers resolve to only **29 unique RenderSurfaces**. Verified sharing
(`docs/url-flags.md` `terrainBc7` row, resolved through `src/lib.rs fetch_terrain_textures`):

| RenderSurface | Shared by |
|---|---|
| `0x06006D6F` | **BarrenRock (0) + Argila (24) + DesolateLands (31)** |
| `0x06006D4D` | WaterRunning (16) + FauxWaterRunning (22) |
| `0x06006D3C` | **PatchyGrassland (9) + Moss (28)** |

Two of those three straddle a family boundary in §1.3 — code 0 is **ROCK** while 24 and 31
are **DIRT**; code 9 and 28 are both GRASS but want different blade heights. **Any effect
keyed off texture identity would treat BarrenRock and DesolateLands as the same biome.**
Key off the terrain code from `terrain_oracle`, always. (This is also the documented
reason `terrain.js` does per-type *vertex* modulation rather than a colour tint for biomes
that share a base texture — see the comment above `DEFAULT_TERRAIN_PALETTE_STRENGTH`.)

#### 2.7.3 Terrain already has parallax occlusion mapping — build on it, don't duplicate

T4 POM is live in the terrain fragment shader (`terrain.js:1196-1197`, march at `:1673`):

```glsl
uniform float uPomEnabled;   // 0.0 OFF / 1.0 ON   — terrain.js:4044, opts.pomEnabled
uniform float uPomScale;     // UV offset amplitude — terrain.js:4045, 0.012
uniform float uPomFadeEnd;   // distance fade
if (uPomEnabled > 0.5 && vViewDepth < uPomFadeEnd && !cellTouchesWater) { … 8 steps … }
```
* 8 dependent atlas taps per fragment; **quality `high`/`ultra` only** (`terrain.js:3136`,
  `:3531`), `?pom=off` escape.
* The height field is the **alpha channel of the atlas** — dominant corner layer.
* **POM offsets `cellUv` before every subsequent sample** (`terrain.js:1658-1693`), and
  everything downstream — albedo, `nra`, alpha masks, TexMerge composite, scroll UV —
  deliberately rides that same offset UV so nothing goes off-registration.
* **Water bypasses POM** (2026-07-31 water-fix, `terrain.js:1663`) via `cellTouchesWater`.

**Consequences for this plan:**
1. **Snow footprints (§3.4) and mud deformation (§3.7) must not re-implement height.** They
   are a *trail-map* term added on top of POM, and they must consume the **POM-offset
   `cellUv`**, not the raw one, or the print will slide against the surface it is denting.
2. **Crack glow (§3.6) and grain sparkle (§3.2) sample after the POM offset** for the same
   reason — read `terrain.js:1720`, which explicitly moved a later stage post-POM to keep
   registration.
3. **Any new terrain-fragment work must honour the `cellTouchesWater` bypass**, or it will
   reintroduce the bug the 07-31 water-fix closed.
4. Because POM is `high`/`ultra` only, effects that lean on it must degrade coherently:
   a `mid`-tier snow print is a darkening term with no displacement, not a broken one.

#### 2.7.4 ⚠ Atlased statics cannot carry custom attributes or material patches

`scene3d/static_atlas.js:690 normalizeForMerge(geom, layer)`:
```js
for (const name of Object.keys(g.attributes)) {
  if (name !== "position" && name !== "normal" && name !== "uv") g.deleteAttribute(name);
}
…
g.setAttribute("aLayer", new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(cnt).fill(layer), 1));
```
`consolidateSingletonsViaTexArray` (`:710`) then **replaces the material** on every atlased
static. **This is exactly why material-level POM silently rendered nothing on statics** —
and why `scene3d/gfx_relief.js` + the Rust `gfx_subdiv.rs` **bake displacement into the
position buffer** instead of patching a material.

**Design rule for every family agent:**
* **Anything you attach to atlased static geometry will be silently erased.** No custom
  vertex attribute, no `onBeforeCompile` patch, no cloned material survives the merge.
* **The terrain mesh is NOT atlased** — it keeps its own `ShaderMaterial` and its full
  attribute set, so terrain-fragment work (sparkle, crack glow, prints) is safe.
* **Standalone meshes you create — grass blades, pebbles, streamer quads, fog billboards,
  particle slot meshes — are not atlased either**, so they are safe.
* If an effect ever *does* need to alter atlased static geometry, the only mechanism is a
  **baked position-buffer change through the Rust path**, i.e. the `gfx_relief` model.
* Independently, `terrain_batch.js:650` whitelists `["position","normal","terrainCode"]`
  (+ optional modulation/lightnormal) and synthesises `aLbSlot` — a new *terrain* attribute
  not on that list vanishes under `?terrainBatch=on` (trap T3). Two different erasure
  mechanisms, same lesson: **prefer uniforms and textures over new attributes.**

#### 2.7.5 If effect config must reach the bake worker, copy the established pattern

The bake work happens in a web worker with **its own wasm instance**, so main-thread
config does not reach it implicitly. The shipped pattern (three sites, copy all three):

```js
// index.html:2200-2208 — main thread resolves ONCE, stashes on globalThis
globalThis.__hbGfxRelief = gfxReliefCfg;

// scene3d/bake_worker_client.js:836 — rides the worker init message
gfxRelief: globalThis.__hbGfxRelief,

// scene3d/bake_worker_client.js:935 — the worker acks it back for diagnosis
if (msg.gfxRelief) globalThis.__hbGfxReliefWorkerAck = msg.gfxRelief;
```
The ack is not decoration — it is how you prove the worker actually got the config rather
than silently running defaults. **Most effects in this plan are render-time and need none
of this**; it applies only if a family adds bake-time data (e.g. a per-LB grass-density
mask computed in Rust). Note also the standing worker trap: the bake worker holds its own
wasm + `init_resource_source(manifest)` and goes **stale after any wasm rebuild or rebake**
until `getBakeWorkerClient().terminate()` or a full reload; the transparent main-thread
fallback means you can silently measure the wrong path (tell: console
`[bake_worker_client] … main-thread fallback`).

#### 2.7.6 Wasm-baked tables

`data/tex-relief-classes.compact.json` is compiled into the wasm via `include_str` —
**any table edit requires a wasm rebuild.** If a family wants a per-terrain relief class,
budget the rebuild. (The v2 classifier pipeline lives at `/mnt/wbterminal2/embed-classify/`;
its LOO reads 0.789 against an enriched, deliberately-boundary seed set — do **not** compare
that number to the older 0.884.)

---

## §3 — The families

`quality.js` facts you need for every family: `PRESET_NAMES = ["low","mid","high","ultra"]`
(:182); `PRESETS` (:21) is a flat object per tier where **every tier carries every key**;
`getQuality(url, userAgent) → {preset, flags, source}` (:396) with URL overrides winning;
coercion sets `BOOL_FLAGS` (:185) / `INT_FLAGS` (:218) / `FLOAT_FLAGS`. Existing particle
cap `maxParticlesPerEmitter`: **low 64 / mid 256 / high 1024 / ultra 2048**.

The canonical runtime read idiom (`particles/particle_emitter.js:213`):
```js
const _qFlags = typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.liveScene3d?.quality?.flags : null;
const cap = Number.isFinite(_qFlags?.myKey) ? _qFlags.myKey : MY_FALLBACK;
```
Add your key to **all four** tiers, add its name to the right coercion set, and document
it in `docs/quality-presets.md` (named as the source of truth at `quality.js:8`).

Perf figures are **budgets**, not measurements — the number to beat on the R9 290 at 25 %
render scale (targets table in `OPTICAL_EFFECTS_HANDOFF.md`). A perf hit is acceptable per
the project owner; a stall is not.

---

### 3.1 GRASS — codes 1, 3, 9, 21, 28, 29 — **flagship**

**The look.** Real blades protruding from the ground, dense near the player, thinning into
the existing detail texture at range; bending as one under the same wind that moves the
trees; **crushed flat where the player walks, springing back over a few seconds.**
Sub-variants: `LushGrass` tall + saturated, `Grassland` medium, `PatchyGrassland` sparse
with bare gaps, `forestfloor` short with leaf-litter tint, `Moss`/`DarkMoss` very short and
near-mat.

**Package verdict: CUSTOM.** No package survives contact.

| Candidate | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `three-grass`, `grass-shader` | **do not exist** | npm registry → `Not found` (2026-07-31) |
| `@react-three/drei` | **FAIL** | peer `react ^19`, `react-dom ^19`, `@react-three/fiber ^9`; no vanilla entry |
| `three-custom-shader-material` `/vanilla` | **REJECT on architecture** | v6.4.0, ESM `./vanilla/…es.js`, peer `three >=0.159` ✓ — compat is fine. But the repo owns a complete injection substrate (`vfx/frag_install.js`, `vfx/vertex_install.js`, `materials.js:432 installVfxComponentPatch`, `materials.js:396 _chainBeforeCompile`, `materials.js:347 _patchSetCacheKey`) with lint enforcement. A second injection philosophy forks the invariant. |
| `simplex-noise@4.0.3` | **OPTIONAL ACCEPT** | ESM `dist/esm/simplex-noise.js`, **zero deps**, no peer. One pin. Only if `wind_rig.js:199 hash01` proves insufficient for clump/lean jitter — prefer no dep. |

Nothing fits because every published grass demo assumes one static ground mesh you own.
AC's ground is a streaming 13×13 ring with LRU evict + park and per-cell terrain types.
The residency logic *is* the hard part, and it is ours.

**Design.** `scene3d/terrain_grass.js`, `scope: "camera"`.

* One `THREE.InstancedMesh`. Blade geometry: 5-vertex strip (4 tris), authored once.
  Per-instance `InstancedBufferAttribute`s written at scatter time, never per frame:
  `aOffset (vec3 world)`, `aRot (float yaw)`, `aScale (vec2 h,w)`, `aTint (vec3)`,
  `aFamilyParam (float sub-variant)`. **No `aHash` attribute needed** — use the existing
  procedural hash: `scene3d/vfx/per_instance.js ensureVfxHashVarying(shader)` derives
  `vVfxHash` from `instanceMatrix[3].xy` / `batchingMatrix[3].xy` / `modelMatrix[3].xy`
  via a `#ifdef` ladder that adds **zero** new programs. If you use it, declare
  `"instanceHash"` in `reads[]`.
* **Placement (CPU, amortised).** Ring buffer of `N` blades; each frame a slice (≤ 512)
  whose distance exceeds `R` is re-scattered on the leading edge: pick `(x,y)` by
  low-discrepancy jitter, `oracle.sample(x,y)`; non-grass family → `aScale.h = 0`
  (degenerate, zero-area, free); else `z = height`, align to `normal`, tint/height from
  the sub-variant table. No frame pays a full re-scatter.
* **Wind (GPU).** Vertex bend from the shared wind phase, using the **same gust function
  as `windSwayGpu.js`** so trees and grass gust together; amplitude cubic in height along
  the blade so the base stays planted. Note `windSwayGpu`'s documented v1 limitation:
  `uWindDir2` is **object-space**. Grass instances share one object frame, so a world-space
  direction is trivially correct here — use it, and note the divergence.
* **STOMP — `scene3d/trail_map.js` (shared, family-agnostic).** One
  `THREE.WebGLRenderTarget`, `R8`/`RG8`, 256², covering `2R × 2R` centred on the player and
  **snapped to a texel grid** so it does not shimmer.
  1. A tiny ortho pass stamps a soft radial blob at the player's (and nearby creatures')
     ground position, additive — a 256² pass with a handful of quads, < 0.1 ms.
  2. Fade toward zero each frame by a constant (recovery ≈ 4 s) via a blended fullscreen
     quad — **never a CPU readback**.
  3. The blade vertex shader samples `uTrailMap` at its own world position, bending the
     blade down proportionally plus a small lateral splay away from the stamp centre.
  * **Ping-pong two RTs** — never read and write the same target in a pass.
  * **Clear on teleport** (`@teleloc`, portal, lifestone) or a stomp scar appears at the
    arrival point. Hook the same seam as the camera/rig teleport snap.
  * At 256² over 96 m that is ~0.37 m/texel — coarse for a single footprint. Snow (§3.4)
    may want a second, smaller, higher-res RT; decide in Wave 2A.
* **Distance blend.** Blades fade to zero scale over the last 20 % of `R`. The terrain
  detail texture underneath is untouched — grass adds, never replaces, so there is no seam.
* **Shadows.** `castShadow = false` at every tier. Rationale is structural, not taste:
  three's `WebGLShadowMap` swaps the **material**, not the geometry, so **added geometry is
  paid in full a second time by the depth pass** — the same reason `gfxSubdivLevel` is 0 on
  every quality tier. `receiveShadow` on the ground is already handled by the CSM patch in
  the terrain material. **Do not add a light.**

**Flags** `?terrainGrass=on|off`, `?terrainGrassDensity=N` (0..2, default 1.0),
`?terrainGrassRadius=N` (m, default 48), `?terrainGrassStomp=on|off` (so the trail RT can
be bisected independently).

**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {blades:24000, radius:32, stomp:false}` ·
`high {blades:60000, radius:48, stomp:true}` ·
`ultra {blades:120000, radius:64, stomp:true}`.

> **Grass is the one effect that breaks the `OPTICAL_EFFECTS_HANDOFF.md` render-scale
> rule.** It is vertex-bound, not fill-bound, so 25 % render scale buys it nothing. The
> degrade lever is **blade count via the quality tier**.
> `scene3d/adaptive_render_scale.js` must **not** drive blade count — leave it owning
> resolution.

**Lifecycle** camera-scoped: no per-LB spawn, no evict/park/rebake handling. The only
interaction is `oracle.sample()` returning `null` for an unbaked LB → those blades stay
degenerate until it lands. On teleport: full (non-amortised) re-scatter + trail-RT clear.

**Perf budget** 60 k blades × 4 tris = 240 k tris, one draw call, no per-frame CPU
transform. ≤ 3.5 ms on R9 290 at `high`. Trail RT ≤ 0.3 ms. Re-scatter CPU ≤ 0.4 ms/frame.

**Tests**
* `test_terrain_grass_scatter.mjs` — **needs real three from `node_modules`**
  (`_three_stub.mjs` has no `InstancedMesh`/`BufferGeometry`; see §6). Deterministic
  scatter for a fixed player pos + seed; non-grass codes → `aScale.h === 0`; a 10 m move
  touches ≤ 512 instances; the instance buffer is allocated exactly once; blade count
  matches the tier.
* `test_terrain_grass_shader.mjs` — pure-ESM, no three: the injected GLSL declares
  `uTrailMap`/wind uniforms **once** (inject over a pre-declared `uniform float uTime;`
  and assert `(fs.match(/uniform float uTime;/g)||[]).length === 1`), is a **no-op when the
  seam is absent** (`shader.vertexShader === before`), is recompile-safe, and does not
  touch the program cache key.
* `test_trail_map.mjs` — texel-quantised snapping (no sub-texel jitter across a 0.01 m
  move); fade reaches < 1/255 within the declared recovery; ping-pong never binds one
  target as both read and write; teleport clears.
* Live — `?nosw=1&terrainGrass=on&autoLogin=1…`, `@telepoi` to a `LushGrass` region,
  `window.__terrainVfx.stats().grass.visibleBlades > 0`, zero console errors, and a
  triangle delta matching the blade count. **Set `renderer.info.autoReset = false` and diff
  cumulative counts** — it defaults true and zeroes per frame.

---

### 3.2 SAND / DESERT — codes 10, 11, 12

**The look.** The surface is *moving*: low sheets of wind-driven sand streaming across the
ground; occasional dust devils; a hazy sun-bleached horizon; grains catching the sun as a
fine grazing-angle sparkle.

**Four effects, descending value:**

1. **Ground-hugging sand streamers.** `scope: "camera"` instanced quad field (≤ 3000),
   each a stretched additively-blended soft streak lying nearly flat
   (`z = height + 0.05..0.4`), advected along the shared wind vector, opacity pulsing on a
   noise field so sheets form and dissolve. Same pool pattern as grass, same oracle gate.
   **Factor the pool out of `terrain_grass.js` into `scene3d/terrain_scatter.js`** in
   Wave 1 so Waves 2-4 reuse it.
2. **Dust devils.** `scope: "landblock"`, ≤ 1 per LB, hash-stable position, built from the
   existing particle system with a rotational velocity term, owned via
   `staticOwnerKeyForLb(lbId)`.
3. **Heat shimmer** — shared with volcano (§3.6).
4. **Grazing-angle grain sparkle** — a fragment addition in the terrain shader gated on
   `FAM_SAND`, reading the code from **`uVertexTypes`** (trap T3). Precedent for the
   maths: `vfx/components/glint.js` + `test_vfx_glint.mjs`.

**Package verdict:**

| Candidate | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `three.quarks@0.17.1` (+ `quarks.core@0.17.1`) | **compat PASS / REJECT on architecture** | ESM `dist/three.quarks.esm.js`, `exports["."].import` ✓, peer `three ">=0.182.0"` → **includes 0.184** ✓. Bare imports are exactly `three` and `quarks.core` (verified by downloading the build — imports on lines 6-8), so **two** pins. `quarks.core` is standalone, zero-dependency ESM (verified: imported clean under `node --input-type=module`, 100 exports). **But** it is a CPU-simulated, batched-instanced particle engine — exactly what `particles/particle_manager.js` already is (`_applyInstancing` :1581, `_finalizeInstBuckets` :1656, `setInstancing` :1621, material pool at :857, RP6 off-screen cull, retail degrade-distance chain). Adopting it bypasses `owner_registry`, the quality cap, the degrade path and the VFX lint. **Shelf it** as the escape hatch if authored/serialised VFX ever become a requirement. |
| `three-nebula@11.1.2` | **REJECT** | ESM `dist/three-nebula.mjs` ✓, peer `three ">=0.122.0 <1.0.0"` ✓ (dev-dep `three ^0.185.1`, actively built against modern three) — but the bundle contains **zero** references to `"three"`: v11 decoupled and requires the host to inject `THREE`. Same duplication objection, weaker perf story (no shared batching with our manager). |
| `@newkrok/three-particles@3.0.0` | **REJECT on compat** | peer `three: "^0.182.0"` — caret on `0.x` means `>=0.182.0 <0.183.0`, **excluding 0.184**. Plus three transitive deps (`@newkrok/three-utils`, `easing-functions`, `three-noise`), each needing its own pin. |

⇒ **Extend the in-repo particle system.** The extension point is *shipped, not
hypothetical*: `scene3d/vfx/components/foliageAmbient.js` already synthesises ambient
emitters from nothing (`foliagePollen` :204, `foliageFireflies` :243, `foliageLeaves` :279,
helper `emitFor` :182) plus `components/breathFog.js`. Descriptor template:

```js
export const foliageFireflies = {
  id: "particle.foliageFireflies",
  family: "particle", mech: "particle", channel: "emitter",
  linkVariant() { return ""; },     // particles add NO shader program
  cacheKeyScope: "none",
  deterministic: true,
  lightCountDelta: 0,               // ← the invariant, declared
  enabled: foliageFirefliesEnabled, // ?visual && ?foliageFireflies
  gateFn: firefliesGate,            // env -> 0..1; gated out => no emitter at all
  spriteName: "softDot",
  reads: ["geometry", "weather", "clock"],
  writes: ["emitter"],
  defaults: { /* full synthesized ParticleEmitterInfo POJO incl. drawRadiusM */ },
  emit(ctx) { return emitFor(this, ctx); },
};
```

**The one thing that differs:** today `ctx.anchor` is a **scenery GfxObj** canopy bbox,
resolved at **bake** time — `docs/url-flags.md` records the consequence for fireflies:
*"gated at BAKE time → appear in landblocks baked/entered at night"*. Terrain-driven
ambients need a **terrain-landblock anchor** evaluated at **LB-ready** time. That is
`terrain_vfx.js`'s job: it builds `ctx.anchor = {partIndex: -1, center: LB centre + mean
height, radius: 96}` and `ctx.seed = lbKey`. **This is a new anchor source, not a new VFX
mechanism** — the descriptors stay in the same registry and pass the same lint.

Supporting infra all exists: `vfx/particle_attach.js` (`particleEntriesForDescriptor`,
`particlePlanForDid`, `isParticleDid`, `staticOwnerKeyForLb`, `attachParticleEmitters`),
`vfx/particle_env.js` (`readParticleEnv`, zero-alloc scratch), `vfx/particle_env_gates.js`,
`vfx/particle_sprites.js` (`PARTICLE_SPRITES` name→DID).

**Flags** `?terrainSand`, `?terrainSandStreamers`, `?terrainSandDevils`,
`?terrainSandSparkle`, shared `?terrainHaze`.
**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {streamers:800, devils:0, sparkle:true}` ·
`high {streamers:2000, devils:1, sparkle:true}` ·
`ultra {streamers:3000, devils:2, sparkle:true}`.
**Lifecycle** streamers camera-scoped; devils landblock-scoped via `ownerRegistry` +
`staticOwnerKeyForLb` — **park stops emission, evict calls `destroyAllForOwner`**.
**Perf budget** streamers ≤ 1.2 ms (additive, fill-bound → *does* scale with render
scale ✓); devils ≤ 0.4 ms; sparkle ≈ 0.2 ms.
**Tests** `test_terrain_sand.mjs` — advection is a pure function of `(wind, clock, hash)`;
a streamer over a non-sand code is culled; devil spawn stable per `lbKey` across two calls;
park leaves `emitterCountForOwner(key)` unchanged; evict calls `destroyAllForOwner` once.

### 3.3 ROCK / BARREN — codes 0, 13, 14, 30

**The look.** Stillness with weight. Hard, dry ground: wind-lifted grit skittering across
the surface, dust where feet land, and — highest value — **scattered pebbles and rubble as
real geometry** so barren ground is not a painted plane.

1. **Instanced pebble/rubble scatter** — `scope: "camera"`, the same
   `terrain_scatter.js` machinery as grass with a different instance mesh (3 pebble shapes
   chosen by hash), much lower density, aligned to `oracle.sample().normal`. Code 30
   (`olthoi`) gets chitinous shards with a faint sickly emissive; 13/14 get flatter shale
   plates. `castShadow = false` (depth-pass doubling, §3.1).
2. **Grit streamers** — the §3.2 streamer module at 1/5 density, greyer, shorter life. A
   parameter block, not a new module.
3. **Footfall dust puffs** — shared with §3.7.

**Package verdict: in-repo.** Same reasoning as grass.

**Flags** `?terrainRock`, `?terrainRockDensity=N`.
**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {pebbles:3000}` · `high {pebbles:9000}` ·
`ultra {pebbles:18000}`.
**Lifecycle** camera-scoped. **Perf budget** ≤ 1.5 ms (opaque + lit, so real fragment
cost).
**Tests** `test_terrain_rock_scatter.mjs` — density scales with tier; instance up-axis
matches `oracle.sample().normal` within 1e-3; olthoi variant only for code 30; zero
pebbles on a grass LB.

### 3.4 SNOW / ICE — codes 2, 15, 27

**The look.** Snow is alive: spindrift ribbons blowing off crests, sun-glitter that
twinkles as the camera moves, footprints that persist, a cold ground-mist in hollows. Ice
(2) and BlueIce (27) instead read hard and wet: sharp specular, low roughness, a hint of
refractive depth, crack detail.

1. **Spindrift ribbons** — the §3.2 streamer system, white, higher-frequency, **biased to
   slope**: spawn preferentially where `oracle.sample().normal` tilts past a threshold,
   which is exactly where real spindrift lifts.
2. **Snow sparkle** — fragment-level in the terrain shader, gated on `FAM_SNOWICE` via
   `uVertexTypes`. Best-precedented effect in the plan: `vfx/components/glint.js` folds
   into `totalEmissiveRadiance` at the `#include <emissivemap_fragment>` seam (*"the first
   seam where `metalnessFactor`, the shading `normal` AND `totalEmissiveRadiance` are all
   resolved"*), binds `uTime` **by reference**, and rides `vVfxHash`. Port that maths with
   a high-frequency **world-space** hash instead of the per-instance one.
   **Camera-motion-dependent twinkle is the whole effect** — a static sparkle texture
   reads as noise.
3. **Footprints** — `trail_map.js` with `recovery = ∞` for snow (prints persist until the
   RT re-centres out of range), sampled as a small downward displacement + darkening.
   Nearly free since the RT already exists. **Must sample at the POM-offset `cellUv`, not
   the raw one** (§2.7.3) or the print slides against the surface it dents, and must honour
   the `cellTouchesWater` bypass. At `mid` (no POM) the print degrades to darkening only —
   a coherent lesser effect, not a broken one.
4. **Ice material treatment** — codes 2/27: roughness ↓, stronger specular, an env term
   from `scene3d/ibl_environment.js`, and a *cheap* fake refraction (offset the detail UV
   by the view vector × a small depth constant). **Explicitly NOT
   `MeshTransmissionMaterial`** — it needs a per-frame scene render into a buffer, i.e. a
   second full world render for a handful of texels. Rejected on cost.
   Note the fake-refraction UV offset stacks with POM's own `cellUv` offset — apply it
   **after** POM and keep the amplitude well under `uPomScale` (0.012) or the two fight.
5. **Ground mist in hollows** — `ground_fog.js` from §3.5, white, thin, low.

**Do not duplicate falling snow.** `scene3d/weather/snow.js` + `weather/manager.js:63
WeatherEffectsManager` already own it (`?snow=on|off` parsed by
`manager.js:30 parseUrlOverrides`, which is the exemplary strict tri-state reader:
`=== "on"` / `=== "off"` / `null`). The manager picks rain vs snow from profile
temperature and forces all precipitation off indoors. This family is the **ground**; read
the weather env so ground spindrift intensifies while it snows.

**Flags** `?terrainSnow`, `?terrainIce` (separate — one is particles+shader, the other a
material change; bisecting matters), `?terrainSnowPrints`.
**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {sparkle:true, spindrift:0, prints:false}` ·
`high {sparkle:true, spindrift:1200, prints:true}` ·
`ultra {sparkle:true, spindrift:2500, prints:true, iceRefraction:true}`.
**Lifecycle** camera-scoped + shader-only ⇒ evict/park-immune.
**Perf budget** sparkle ≈ 0.3 ms; spindrift ≤ 1.0 ms; prints ≈ 0; ice ≈ 0.2 ms.
**Tests** `test_terrain_snow.mjs` — sparkle GLSL declares uniforms once, **binds the shared
clock by identity** (`shader.uniforms.uTime === VFX_GLOBALS.uTime`, the exact assertion in
`test_vfx_glint.mjs`), reads a world-space hash, writes only emissive, leaves the program
key alone. `test_terrain_ice.mjs` — material params change for codes 2/27 only; **scene
light count unchanged** across install/uninstall.

### 3.5 SWAMP / MARSH — code 4 (+ 23, contested — §3.8.3)

**The look.** Oppressive and damp: fireflies drifting at night, sluggish marsh gas
bubbling and occasionally igniting as a wisp, low fog clinging *in* the terrain, midge
swarms in shafts of light.

1. **Fireflies — ALREADY EXIST; re-anchor them.** `vfx/components/foliageAmbient.js:243
   foliageFireflies` (`particleType: PT_SWARM`, `cos(b·t)*C` hover, `particle.js:231`;
   note its own comment that it *"MUST be an additive sprite (Surface 0x10000)"*), gate
   `particle_env_gates.js firefliesGate`, flag `vfx_flags.js:200 foliageFirefliesEnabled`,
   seasonal relaxation `?foliageStrictSeason`. Today they anchor to tree canopies. **Do not
   write a second firefly system** — add the terrain anchor source so `FAM_SWAMP`
   landblocks emit them from the ground at night, marsh-green and lower-drifting.
2. **Marsh gas** — `scope: "landblock"`, a few stationary bubble emitters at hash-stable
   positions in the LB's swamp cells. Rare ignition (a ~2 s wisp) on a long timer.
   **Must not add a light** (§5.2) — fake the glow with an additive sprite.
3. **Ground fog** — new shared `scene3d/ground_fog.js`: a camera-centred ring of ~24 large
   soft horizontal billboards at `z = height + 0.2..1.5`, depth-write off, soft-particle
   fade against the depth buffer. **Depth caveat:** log-encoded (trap T4) **and** the R9 290
   HalfFloat/LINEAR regression — use NEAREST with a sentinel-aware threshold, per
   `OPTICAL_EFFECTS_HANDOFF.md`.
4. **Midge swarms** — reuse `foliagePollen` (:204) with a swamp tint and tighter orbit.

**Package verdict:**

| Candidate | Result |
|---|---|
| `three-good-godrays@0.12.0` | **REJECT on compat.** ESM ✓ (`build/three-good-godrays.esm.js`, `type: module`), peer `postprocessing ^6.33.4` ✓ — but peer `three ">= 0.125.0 <= 0.182.0"` **excludes 0.184**; the upper bound is deliberate. For shafts use pmndrs' own `GodRaysEffect` (already in the pinned `postprocessing@6.39.1`), fully scoped with a wiring recipe and quality table in `OPTICAL_EFFECTS_HANDOFF.md` §2. |
| `three-volumetric-pass` | **Not on npm** under that name (`Not found`); GitHub-only. Vendoring means owning a raymarched volumetric pass; `@takram/three-clouds` is already vendored for volumetrics. **Reject** — build the billboard fog. |
| in-repo billboards + existing particle system | **ACCEPT** |

**Flags** `?terrainSwamp`, `?terrainGroundFog` (shared with snow/volcano), `?terrainMarshGas`.
**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {fog:8, gas:false, fireflies:true}` ·
`high {fog:16, gas:true, fireflies:true}` · `ultra {fog:24, gas:true, wisps:true}`.
**Lifecycle** fog camera-scoped; gas + fireflies landblock-scoped via `ownerRegistry` +
`staticOwnerKeyForLb`; park stops emission, evict destroys.
**Perf budget** fog ≤ 1.5 ms (fill-bound, scales ✓); gas ≤ 0.3 ms.
**Tests** `test_terrain_swamp.mjs` — the terrain anchor produces a firefly emitter spec
byte-identical to the canopy path except anchor/tint (proving reuse, not a fork); gas
positions stable per `lbKey`; `lightCountDelta === 0` on every synthesised component; a new
gate fn added to `particle_env_gates.js` is covered by the same shape checks
`test_vfx_foliage.mjs` applies. `test_ground_fog.mjs` — billboards face the camera, never

### 3.6 VOLCANO / OBSIDIAN — codes 6, 25, 26

**The look.** Dangerous. Heat visibly distorting the air, embers lifting and dying, a dull
red glow breathing in the cracks underfoot, ash drifting down, obsidian glassy-black with a
hard specular edge.

1. **Heat shimmer — a custom pmndrs `Effect`.** The one place a postprocessing addition is
   clearly right. API confirmed for v6:
   ```js
   super("HeatHazeEffect", fragmentShader, {
     blendFunction: BlendFunction.NORMAL,
     attributes: EffectAttribute.DEPTH,
     uniforms: new Map([["uTime", new Uniform(0)], ["uHeatCenter", new Uniform(new Vector3())],
                        ["uHeatRadius", new Uniform(0)], ["hbLogDepthFC", new Uniform(0)]]),
   });
   ```
   Shader implements `void mainUv(inout vec2 uv)` (the cheapest effect class — a pure UV
   warp) and/or the depth form
   `void mainImage(const in vec4 inputColor, const in vec2 uv, const in float depth, out vec4 outputColor)`.
   **Decode the log depth** (trap T4); `HorizonDissolveEffect`
   (`atmosphere_pipeline.js:141`) is the working in-tree template, including its
   `window.__horizonFade` live-tuning handle — copy that pattern for the 1070 eye-test.
   **Insert into the EXISTING `EffectPass`, never a new pass.** Construction site,
   `atmosphere_pipeline.js:524`:
   ```js
   const fxPass = new EffectPass(camera,
     ...[aerialPerspective, horizonDissolve, lensFlare, bloom, vignette, toneMapping, dithering].filter(Boolean));
   ```
   Ordering rule quoted at `:520`: everything except ToneMapping + Dithering operates in
   HDR space; Vignette before ToneMapping; ToneMapping after LensFlare, before Dithering.
   **Put heat haze first**, before `aerialPerspective`, so the distortion is applied to the
   raw scene and then correctly fogged. Pass `null` when disabled so `filter(Boolean)`
   drops the slot — no extra blit. Composer buffer is `THREE.HalfFloatType`
   (`atmosphere_pipeline.js:274`).
   **Masking:** do not add a mask pass. v1 takes `uHeatCenter` / `uHeatRadius` (the nearest
   volcanic LB) from `terrain_vfx.js` and reconstructs world position from depth.
   **Zero `uHeatRadius` when no volcanic LB is resident**, or the distortion follows the
   player out of the region.
2. **Embers — re-anchor, don't rewrite.** `vfx/components/brazierEmbers.js` exists and is
   covered by `test_brazier_emit.mjs`. Give it a terrain anchor with a wider footprint,
   landblock-scoped, hash-stable.
3. **Crack glow** — terrain fragment: for `FAM_VOLCANO`, an emissive term modulated by a
   high-frequency world-space noise threshold and a slow breathing oscillator. Use the
   registered oscillator infra: `vfx/oscillators.js` (`WAVES` = `{sine, triangle,
   smoothNoise, decay}`, `sampleWave`, `registerOscillator`, `tickOscillators`). Note
   `tickOscillators` **wraps the clock at 3600 s** (`t = tSec % 3600`) to bound float32
   drift — phase-continuous for any ≤ 1 Hz waveform, so keep your frequencies there.
   Pairs with `BloomEffect`, already constructed at `atmosphere_pipeline.js:499` and gated
   by `quality.flags.bloom`.
4. **Ash fall** — a camera-scoped downward drifter. **Check whether
   `scene3d/weather/snow.js SnowSystem` can be parameterised** before writing a third
   falling-particle system (`rain.js`, `snow.js` already exist).
5. **Obsidian material** — code 6: roughness ↓↓, dark tight specular; same mechanism as the
   ice treatment.

> Note: `TERRAIN_LAVA_CODES` (`terrain.js:793`) is **empty** for Region `0x13`, so the
> vertex shader's lava-displacement branch never fires in Dereth. Volcanic terrain today
> is visually just dark stone — which is exactly why this family has so much headroom.

**Package verdict:** `postprocessing@6.39.1` — **already pinned**. No new package.

**Flags** `?terrainVolcano`, `?terrainHaze` (shared with sand), `?terrainEmbers`,
`?terrainCrackGlow`.
**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {crackGlow:true}` ·
`high {crackGlow:true, haze:true, embers:1}` ·
`ultra {crackGlow:true, haze:true, embers:3, ash:true}`.
**Lifecycle** embers/ash landblock-scoped (park-aware); haze + crack glow are
screen/shader effects with no per-LB state beyond the `uHeatRadius` clear.
**Perf budget** haze ≤ 1.0 ms at 25 % scale (fill-bound ✓); embers ≤ 0.5 ms; crack glow
≈ 0.2 ms.
**Tests** `test_terrain_volcano.mjs` — the Effect constructs with `EffectAttribute.DEPTH`,
exposes `mainUv`, decodes log depth (source-scan for `exp2(`), is inserted into the
**existing** `fxPass` (assert `composer.passes.length` unchanged), binds the shared clock
by identity, and `uHeatRadius → 0` with no volcanic LB resident. Ember re-anchor produces
the same emitter spec as the brazier path modulo anchor.

### 3.7 DIRT / MUD — codes 5, 7, 8, 24, 31

**The look.** Ground that responds: footfall dust on dry dirt; wet, glossy, deforming mud
that keeps footprints and slowly heals; wind-lifted dry dust on `DesolateLands`; clay
(`Argila`) redder and slicker after rain.

1. **Footfall puffs** — a small burst emitter on ground contact, colour picked from
   `oracle.sample().code`. **Hang off the existing footstep-audio trigger** rather than
   re-deriving contact from velocity.
2. **Mud footprints + wetness** — `trail_map.js` with slow recovery (~30 s), driving both a
   small vertex displacement and a roughness/specular change. Same POM-registration rule as
   snow prints (§2.7.3): sample at the POM-offset `cellUv`, honour `cellTouchesWater`, and
   degrade to darkening-only below the POM tier. **Reuse the response curve
   from `vfx/components/wetness.js`** (covered by `test_vfx_wetness.mjs`) so puddled
   statics and puddled ground agree. The smoothed driver already exists:
   `weather_inputs.js frostTarget/wetntargets` write `VFX_GLOBALS.uWetness` /
   `uFrost` with `FROST_TAU`/`WET_TAU` exponential approach, `dt = Infinity` on the first
   frame so boot snaps, `dt` clamped for tab-resume spikes.
3. **Dry dust haze** — the §3.2 streamer system, brown, very low, `DesolateLands` biased.
4. **Rain interaction** — read `getWeatherInputs().wetness`; do not re-derive from
   `weather/rain.js`.

**Package verdict: in-repo only.**

**Flags** `?terrainDirt`, `?terrainFootfall`, `?terrainMudPrints`.
**Tiers** `low: null` · `mid {footfall:true}` ·
`high {footfall:true, prints:true, dustHaze:800}` ·
`ultra {footfall:true, prints:true, dustHaze:2000, wetness:true}`.
**Lifecycle** camera/player-scoped throughout. **Perf budget** ≤ 0.8 ms total.
**Tests** `test_terrain_dirt.mjs` — puff colour follows the sampled code; no puff on a
water/ice code; print recovery monotonic; wetness tracks `VFX_GLOBALS.uWetness` with the
documented lag; no light added.

### 3.8 WATER (16-20, 22) and SeaSlime (23) — EXCLUDED; interaction contract

1. **Never place on a water code.** Every scatter/emitter path filters
   `family !== FAM_WATER` before placing. `test_terrain_oracle.mjs` asserts the membership;
   each family test asserts zero placements.
2. **Shorelines are shared.** Grass, sand and mud will all sample cells adjacent to water.
   The oracle's `cornerCodes` exists so a family can *feather* — fade to zero over the last
   metre before a water corner — without either agent needing the other's code.
3. **Code 23 (`SeaSlime`) — RESOLVED IN THE WATER AGENT'S FAVOUR, by default.**
   `terrain.js:788 TERRAIN_WATER_CODES` ships `{16,17,18,19,20,22,23}`, so the client
   already treats 23 (and 22) as water, and the vertex shader gives them wave
   displacement via `uWaterCodeMask`. `?strictWaterCodes` **drops** 22 and 23.
   **Therefore: `FAM_WATER` includes 23 by default; the swamp family picks 23 up only when
   `?strictWaterCodes` is set.** Derive this from `TERRAIN_WATER_CODES` at runtime — do not
   hardcode. The swamp agent should still confirm with the water agent before shipping the
   strict-mode branch.

## §4 — Package delivery and the full verdict table

### 4.1 How a package gets in

Two mechanisms only (`index.html` importmap block ≈:957; `VENDORED.md`):

**(a) importmap CDN pin** — small, stable, dependency-light ESM:
```html
"three":           "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.184.0/build/three.module.js",
"three/addons/":   "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.184.0/examples/jsm/",
"postprocessing":  "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/postprocessing@6.39.1/build/index.js",
"tiny-invariant":  "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tiny-invariant@1.3.3/dist/esm/tiny-invariant.js"
```
**(b) vendored ESM under `vendor/`** — anything patched, large, or with transitive deps:
`"@takram/three-clouds": "./vendor/takram-three-clouds/build/index.js"`.

A pin is legal only if **every transitive bare specifier** is itself pinned. That is why
`three.quarks` costs two pins and `@newkrok/three-particles` costs four.

### 4.2 Verdict table (all verified 2026-07-31)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `postprocessing` | 6.39.1 | already pinned | — | ✓ | **USE** — custom `Effect` for heat haze; `Bloom`/`GodRays` pre-scoped in `OPTICAL_EFFECTS_HANDOFF.md` |
| `three` + `three/addons/` | 0.184.0 | already pinned | — | ✓ | **USE** freely |
| `simplex-noise` | 4.0.3 | `dist/esm/simplex-noise.js` | none (0 deps) | ✓ | **OPTIONAL** — 1 pin. Only if `wind_rig.js:199 hash01` is insufficient |
| `three.quarks` (+ `quarks.core`) | 0.17.1 | `dist/three.quarks.esm.js` | `>=0.182.0` | ✓ | **COMPAT PASS / REJECT on architecture** — duplicates `particle_manager.js`; 2 pins. Shelved |
| `three-nebula` | 11.1.2 | `dist/three-nebula.mjs` | `>=0.122.0 <1.0.0` | ✓ | **REJECT** — same duplication; host must inject `THREE`; no shared batching |
| `@newkrok/three-particles` | 3.0.0 | `dist/index.js` | `^0.182.0` | ✗ | **REJECT** — semver excludes r184; 3 transitive deps |
| `three-good-godrays` | 0.12.0 | `build/…esm.js` | `>=0.125.0 <=0.182.0` | ✗ | **REJECT** — explicit upper bound below r184; use pmndrs `GodRaysEffect` |
| `three-volumetric-pass` | — | — | — | — | **REJECT** — not published to npm under that name |
| `three-custom-shader-material` | 6.4.0 | `vanilla/…es.js` | `>=0.159` | ✓ | **REJECT on architecture** — competes with `vfx/frag_install.js` + `lint_caps.js` |
| `@react-three/drei` | 10.7.7 | — | `>=0.159` | ✓ | **REJECT** — React-only |
| `three-mesh-bvh` | 0.9.13 | `src/index.js` | `>=0.159.0` | ✓ | **NOT NEEDED** — `terrainHeightAt` + the JS split-triangle port cover ground queries. Reserve only if arbitrary-mesh raycasts become necessary |
| `@takram/three-clouds` | 0.7.6 (vendored) | `vendor/takram-three-clouds/build/index.js` | `>=0.170.0` | ✓ | **IN USE** — its npm peers list React packages; the vendored build is used vanilla, which is why it is vendored not pinned |

**Net: this programme adds at most ONE new pin (`simplex-noise`), probably zero.** That is
the correct outcome — the repo's particle, VFX-substrate, wind, weather and postprocessing
infrastructure is more capable and better integrated than anything on npm for this job.

## §5 — Invariants (three are mechanically enforced and will throw)

**5.1 The read/write firewall.** `scene3d/vfx/lint_caps.js` header states THE RULE: *"a
component READS only static/derived inputs + the client clock; WRITES only render-time
transforms / cloned-material uniforms the server neither stores nor replicates; NEVER the
wire value, physics/collision, or a server-replicated field."* The vocabulary is exact:
```js
ALLOWED_READS  = {geometry, surface, setup, weenieProps, serverPose,
                  instanceHash, clock, drawCastSubstate, weather}
ALLOWED_WRITES = {renderTransform, partTransform, materialUniform, emitter, lightIntensity}
FORBIDDEN_READS  = {serverReplicated, otherEntityState, wireInbound}
FORBIDDEN_WRITES = {wire, physics, collision, replicatedPose, lightCount}
```
Three enforcement layers: **A** `lintManifest(c)` — also enforced hard at registration
(`vfx/registry.js:62 registerComponent` **throws**); **B** `lintSource(sourceText)` — a
regex denylist over comment-stripped source; **C** `test_vfx_legacy_safety.mjs`.
Layer B is a **per-component test responsibility**: read your own file off disk and run it.

**5.2 Never change the scene light count.** `vfx/registry.js:40 validateComponent`:
```js
if (c?.lightCountDelta !== 0)
  errs.push("lightCountDelta must be 0 (never change visible light count -> relink freeze)");
```
Root cause in `scene3d/lighting.js:50`/`:404` — MeshStandardMaterial recompiles when light
counts change; the light pool exists precisely so *"the renderer's per-type light count
NEVER changes → no shader relink → no freeze"* (`lighting.js:1795`). `scene3d/csm.js`
`setupCsm` **throws** unless `splits.length === 3` and `mapSizes.length === 3`; its three
`DirectionalLight`s are constructed at **intensity 0** as pure shadow projectors.
Glowing things (wisps, embers, crack glow, firefly bodies) are **emissive/additive sprites
and fragment terms**, never `PointLight`s.

**5.3 `.visible = ` is banned in VFX component source.** `lint_caps.js FORBIDDEN_SOURCE`
denies it outright — *"use intensity=0, never `.visible=`"* — along with
`wasmExports.(enqueue|send)*`, `wasmExports.*Collision*`, `.setPosition|moveTo|teleport(`,
`Math.random(`, argless `Date.now()`, and `customProgramCacheKey…(guid|instanceHash|
aVfxHash)`. Escape hatch: a raw line carrying `// vfx-lint-allow: <reason>`.
**Practical consequence for this plan:** host modules (`terrain_vfx.js`, `terrain_grass.js`)
are not registered components and are not lint-swept, so they may toggle mesh visibility —
but **registered components must stop emission or set intensity to 0**, never
`.visible = false`. Keep park-time visibility churn in the host module.

**5.4 Never vary the program cache key per instance.** `validateComponent`:
```js
if (c?.cacheKeyScope !== "set" && c?.cacheKeyScope !== "none")
  errs.push('cacheKeyScope must be "set"|"none", never "instance" (shader-link explosion)');
```
`materials.js:347 _patchSetCacheKey` builds the key from *set membership* only
(`"|v" + userData.__vfxSetKey`, empty string when unpatched ⇒ key unchanged for every
existing material). Per-instance variety goes through `ensureVfxHashVarying` (a varying
derived from the instance matrix — zero CPU, zero new programs) or an
`InstancedBufferAttribute`. Guards: `test_visfid_c4_program_cache_key.mjs`,
`test_vfx_per_instance_hash.mjs`.

**5.5 Determinism.** Placement is a pure function of `(lbKey or world cell, hash, tier)`.
`Math.random()` is lint-banned; use `wind_rig.js:199 hash01` or a seeded PRNG. This is what
makes park/unpark and rebake invisible and the node tests possible. The particle system
even has an injectable determinism seam: `particles/time_rng.js` (`setCurrentTime`,
`setRng`).

**5.6 Bind the clock by reference.** `uTime` is `VFX_GLOBALS.uTime`, not a clone. Assert by
**identity**, as `test_vfx_glint.mjs` does. `linkVariant() { return ""; }` unless you truly
need distinct GLSL. `declareUniforms` must be idempotent (`_ensureUniformDecl`) —
redeclaring `uTime` across a component SET is a GLSL error.

**5.7 Added geometry is paid twice.** three's shadow map swaps the **material**, not the
geometry. VFX material clones are colour-pass-only (`__vfxColorPassOnly`, guarded by
`vfx/shadow_guard.js assertNoVfxDepthLeak` / `projectDepthMaterial` /
`assertDepthMaterialUnpatched`) and are free, but any geometry a family adds costs the
depth pass as well. Shadows are ~half the GPU cost at `quality=high`. **Set
`castShadow = false` on every scatter mesh in this plan.**

**5.8 Degrade with quality; know which lever.** Add a key to all four `PRESETS` tiers, add
its name to the correct coercion set, document it in `docs/quality-presets.md`. **`low` is
`null`/disabled for every effect here without exception.** Fill-bound effects (fog, haze,
streamers) get cheaper at 25 % render scale automatically; vertex-bound effects (grass,
pebbles) do not — their lever is instance count.

**5.9 Ship OFF, promote deliberately.** `_boolFlag(name, false)` at ship time; the
`=off` escape hatch stays forever after promotion (house rule in `docs/url-flags.md`).

**5.10 Stale-build discipline.** `?nosw=1` on **every** dev URL — the service worker caches
`index.html`, `/shards/` and `boot.hba` across reloads and **`Ctrl+Shift+R` does not clear
it**. Touching `crates/` or `src/lib.rs` requires a wasm rebuild; a `--dev` wasm is ~4×
slower than `--release`, so never benchmark against one.
