## §6 — Validation bar (what "done" means)

1. **Node tests green.** No test framework, no `package.json` — run directly:
   ```
   cd apps/holtburger-web/
   node test_terrain_grass_scatter.mjs
   ```
   Structure (copy `test_vfx_glint.mjs`): a `// Locks: …` header enumerating the
   invariants; import the component **for its registration side effect**; a
   `check(label, cond, extra)` helper printing `[OK]`/`[FAIL]`; a summary line;
   `if (failed > 0) process.exit(1);`.

   **Choose the right three tier:**
   * **Pure-ESM, no three** (preferred) — `oscillators.js`, `lint_caps.js`, `registry.js`,
     `per_instance.js`, `frag_install.js`, `frag_attach.js`, `particle_attach.js` are all
     deliberately THREE-free leaf modules. **Keep `terrain_families.js`, `terrain_oracle.js`
     and the shader-string builders THREE-free for the same reason.**
   * **Real three from `node_modules`** — needed for anything touching `InstancedMesh`,
     `BufferGeometry`, `WebGLRenderTarget`. Precedents: `test_particle_billboard.mjs`,
     `test_vfx_material_substrate.mjs`.
   * **Stubbed three** — `_three_stub.mjs` exports only `Vector3, Quaternion, Object3D,
     Mesh, SphereGeometry, TorusGeometry, BoxGeometry, MeshBasicMaterial, AdditiveBlending,
     FrontSide, DoubleSide`. **It has no `InstancedMesh` and no `BufferGeometry`** — it will
     not carry a grass test. Register it via
     `module.register(pathToFileURL(resolve(__dirname, "../_three_stub_loader.mjs")).href)`.
     Extended variants exist for terrain: `_three_stub_palette.mjs` +
     `_three_stub_palette_loader.mjs` (used by `test_terrain_palette.mjs`,
     `test_terrain_detail_tex.mjs`, `test_terrain_texmerge.mjs`) — **check whether the
     palette stub covers your needs before adding a third stub.**

   (`run-all-validators.cjs` runs `validate_*.cjs`, **not** `test_*.mjs` — don't expect it
   to pick your test up.)
2. **`node scripts/lint-url-flags.mjs --app apps/holtburger-web` exits 0.**
3. **Bare-default boot is byte-unchanged.** Flag absent ⇒ identical behaviour. Prove it:
   boot with and without the module imported; diff console output and `renderer.info` draw
   calls. This is the same guarantee `resolveFragMaterial` gives by returning `null`.
4. **Live headless smoke — BOTH texture arms.** Logic/perf can run on either; the **look**
   is signed off on the BC7 arm only.
   * **Plain / CC0 arm** — `scripts/serve.py` on **:8765**, flags
     `?nosw=1&<flag>=on&autoLogin=1&account=…&password=…&autoSpawn=first&agent=1`.
   * **BC7 look-target arm** — `/mnt/wbterminal2/bc7-v2-rebake/serve/serve-hires-bc7.sh`
     on **:8767**, and **hardcode both texture flags into the URL**:
     `?nosw=1&texBc7=on&terrainBc7=on&<flag>=on&…`. Both are strict exact-match opt-ins;
     omitting them is exactly how the 07-30 showcase silently shot the plain dist.
     ⚠ `--check` passing does **not** prove the URL serves the right dist — the webroot's
     `apps/holtburger-web/dist` symlink is what the path resolves through. Verify with
     `curl` on `dist/manifest/holtburger-tex-bc7.bin` before trusting a shot.
   Then: poll `window.__bootState === 'in-world'`; `@telepoi` to a region with your terrain
   family; assert zero console errors, non-zero work in `window.__terrainVfx.stats()`, and a
   60-frame `renderer.info` delta within budget. `?nullRender=1` for logic-only runs.
   SwiftShader can leave `__bootState === 'error'` on the 90 s `scene-ready` timeout with a
   perfectly fine scene — proceed once mesh count > 100.
   Also run one arm at `?quality=mid` to confirm the **POM-off degrade path** (§2.7.3)
   renders a coherent lesser effect rather than a broken one.
   (ACE runs locally on 9000/9001; if earlyoom kills it, restart via
   `/mnt/wbterminal2/ace-logs/start-ace.sh`.)
5. **Eye-test batching.** Real-GPU validation happens on the GTX-1070 box, batched:
   develop flagged-off, queue the URL flags, one off-screen session. Never take that
   machine's screen.
6. **Only then** flip the default and update the `Default` **and `Reader`** cells in
   `docs/url-flags.md`.

## §7 — Wave plan (2 implementation agents per wave)

Standing rules for every wave: any agent editing the **terrain fragment shader** (1B, 2A,
2B) must first read §2.7.3 and place its work relative to the POM `cellUv` offset and the
`cellTouchesWater` bypass; any agent adding a **terrain geometry attribute** must update the
`terrain_batch.js:650` whitelist; **nobody** touches atlased static geometry (§2.7.4). All
look validation happens on the **:8767 BC7 arm with `texBc7=on&terrainBc7=on` hardcoded**.

### WAVE 0 — foundation (BLOCKS EVERYTHING; both items must land together)

| Agent | Scope | New files | Touched files |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0A** | Terrain oracle + families | `scene3d/terrain_families.js`, `scene3d/terrain_oracle.js`, `test_terrain_families.mjs`, `test_terrain_oracle.mjs` | `scene3d/terrain.js` — **one line**: add `heights: Float32Array.from(wasmMesh.heights)` to the `lbMesh.userData` literal (:4139) |
| **0B** | VFX spine + flags + trail map | `scene3d/terrain_vfx.js`, `scene3d/trail_map.js`, `test_terrain_vfx_lifecycle.mjs`, `test_trail_map.mjs` | `scene3d/vfx_flags.js` (readers + `VFX_EFFECT_FLAGS` rows), `docs/url-flags.md` (rows with Reader column), `scene3d/quality.js` (keys in all 4 tiers + coercion sets), `docs/quality-presets.md`, `scene3d/loop.js` (one `terrainVfxTick(dt, ctx)` call next to `tickVfxOscillators` at :949), `scene3d/index.js` (construct, install the three-facade hooks, expose `window.__terrainVfx`) |

0B writes against the documented oracle API with a stub so both can proceed in parallel.
**Wave 0 exit criterion:** `window.__terrainVfx.oracleSelfTest()` passes live, and the
park-survival test is green.

### WAVE 1 — the two that change the game

| Agent | Scope | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| **1A** | **§3.1 GRASS** — `scene3d/terrain_grass.js`, plus factoring the reusable `scene3d/terrain_scatter.js` out of it; stomp via `trail_map.js`. Flags `terrainGrass`, `terrainGrassDensity`, `terrainGrassRadius`, `terrainGrassStomp`. | Wave 0 |
| **1B** | **§3.2 SAND** — `scene3d/terrain_sand.js` (streamers, dust devils, grain sparkle). Flags `terrainSand`, `terrainSandStreamers`, `terrainSandDevils`, `terrainSandSparkle`. | Wave 0 |

**Sequencing:** 1A lands `terrain_scatter.js` as its **own first commit** — a pure, tested,
effect-agnostic instanced-scatter pool — then both proceed. **Only 1B touches the terrain
fragment shader this wave** (the sand sparkle); 1A's shader work is entirely in its own
grass material. 1B must also update the `terrain_batch.js:650` attribute whitelist if it
adds a terrain geometry attribute (trap T3).

## §8 — Open risks and unknowns

1. **Subdivision vs the 81-vertex height grid.** The subdiv mesh path is live for all LBs
   (`userData.subdivLevel` ∈ {1,2,4,8}; geometry becomes `(subdiv*8+1)²`). Both
   `terrainHeightAt` and the JS port interpolate the **base 9×9** grid. `src/lib.rs:35075`
   claims it "tracks the exact drawn surface"; the shader additionally applies
   `ZFIGHT_TERRAIN_ADJUST_M` (`?terrainLower`, default ~0.01 m) and water displacement.
   **Verify against a subdivided LB before trusting grass grounding**; if it drifts, fall
   back to a `THREE.Raycaster` against `lbMesh` for blade grounding only.
2. **Nearest-vertex code snapping is coarse at 24 m.** `ambient_runtime.js:646` documents
   this as a deliberate simplification for audio, where it is fine. For *visual* effects a
   24 m quantisation produces visible square patches at type boundaries. The GPU
   bilinear-blends the four corner *textures* (`terrain.js:1570-1638`), so a nearest-vertex
   sample and the rendered pixel actively disagree near cell edges. Mitigation is
   `cornerCodes` + hash-dithered blending. **This is the highest-risk visual unknown in the
   plan — Wave 1A must prototype it before blade art.**
3. **Match the shader's own boundary rule.** `terrain.js`'s `texMerge` path keys detail
   layers off *"the nearest-corner code, not flat `vTerrainCode`"*. Grass placement should
   match, or blades will disagree with the ground texture under them.
4. **Park storm.** `test_landblock_lru_park_storm.mjs` exists, so park churn is a known
   failure mode. Landblock-scoped providers must be cheap to park/unpark; if any provider's
   unpark cost is non-trivial, prefer camera scope.
5. **Heat-haze masking.** The v1 single-`uHeatCenter` approach will look wrong where
   volcanic and non-volcanic LBs interleave. Accepted for v1; the proper fix (a heat channel
   written by the terrain fragment shader) needs a spare render-target channel that has not
   been surveyed.
6. **Grass vertex budget on the R9 290.** 60 k blades at `high` is a hypothesis, not a
   result. It may need to be 25 k. Measure before fixing the tier table.
7. **Trail-map resolution.** 256² over 96 m ≈ 0.37 m/texel — coarse for one footprint. Snow
   may want a second smaller high-res RT. Decide in Wave 2A.
8. **`?wireframe=1` must be a no-op.** Wireframe skips sky/composer/CSM/shadows and uses
   `MeshBasicMaterial`; `terrain_batch` explicitly never batches in that mode. Put the guard
   in `terrain_vfx.js` **once**, not per family.
9. **Falling-particle triplication.** `weather/rain.js`, `weather/snow.js` and a proposed
   ash-fall all do the same thing. Wave 2B should parameterise `SnowSystem` rather than
   write a third; if that proves invasive, note it and move on — the owner has explicitly
   deferred refactoring.
10. **`VFX_GLOBALS.uCamPos` is dead.** Declared in `materials.js:415`, written by nothing.
    Any family needing a camera/player world position in a *terrain* shader must wire it
    (trap T2) and own the consequence.
11. **The terrain material's `uWindDir` is dead** (trap T1). Wiring it live changes the sand
    UV rotation at `terrain.js:2050-2070` — a visual change to an existing shipped surface,
    so it needs its own flag and eye-test, not a silent fix.
12. **Region generality.** `terrain_palette.json` is Dereth (`0x13000000`). Other regions
    could name codes differently. Not a practical risk today, but the family LUT must be
    **code-indexed, never name-matched**.
13. **Tuning against the wrong texture arm.** Colours, sparkle thresholds and emissive
    strengths tuned on the CC0 arm (:8765 default) will read wrong on the BC7 arm (:8767),
    which is the look target. Retail BC7 albedo is materially different in value and
    saturation from the curated ambientCG art. **Tune on :8767 with `texBc7=on&terrainBc7=on`
    hardcoded**; re-check on :8765 only for "does it still make sense", not for calibration.
    Second-order risk: a GPU without `EXT_texture_compression_bptc` silently falls back to
    the CC0 arm, so a BC7-calibrated effect must not look broken there.
14. **POM registration drift.** Snow prints, mud prints, crack glow and grain sparkle all
    add fragment work to a shader whose UVs are already parallax-offset. Getting the
    offset order wrong produces a subtle slide that is easy to miss in a still and obvious
    in motion — i.e. exactly the class of bug the 07-30 showcase critique was about
    ("effects seem random"). **Validate every new terrain-fragment effect in motion, on the
    1070, not from a screenshot.** POM is also `high`/`ultra` only, so each effect needs a
    deliberate `mid` degrade.
15. **Someone will try to patch an atlased static.** §2.7.4 is counter-intuitive — a
    material patch that works everywhere else silently does nothing on atlased statics
    because `normalizeForMerge` strips attributes and the consolidator replaces the
    material. Nothing in this plan targets atlased statics today, but "make the mossy
    stones sparkle too" is an obvious next request and the answer is a baked Rust
    position-buffer change, not a material patch.
16. **`instanceHash` on a camera-scoped pool.** `ensureVfxHashVarying` derives the hash from
    `instanceMatrix[3].xy` — i.e. the instance's **current** position. For a re-scattering
    grass pool the hash therefore changes when a blade moves, which is *desirable* (the
    blade genuinely becomes a different blade) but means the hash cannot be used as a
    stable per-blade identity across re-scatter. Use an explicit
    `InstancedBufferAttribute` if stable identity is ever needed.
